rules.reason: Early trigger causes Coolify to pull the previous stale image instead of the newly built one.
rules.rule: Coolify webhook redeploy trigger must fire after the GHCR image push completes, not before.

rules.reason: Floating tags (e.g. actions/checkout@main) can be updated by the action author and introduce unexpected behavior.
rules.rule: Pin SHA or version tags for all third-party GitHub Actions steps.

rules.reason: Coolify probes the internal container network. Using the public domain adds unnecessary DNS round-trips and can fail if DNS hasn't propagated.
rules.rule: Coolify health checks must target 127.0.0.1, not the public domain.

rules.reason: Coolify health probes do not send credentials. A protected health endpoint will always return 401 and Coolify will mark the app as unhealthy.
rules.rule: If an app uses Basic Auth, exempt the health check path (/api/health) from authentication.

rules.reason: The registry only stays current if agents and humans update it. A stale registry is worse than no registry.
rules.rule: Write back to Infra Brain when a new version is validated or a new lesson is learned.

rules.reason: 8 of 10 apps already use main. Standardized March 2026 audit.
rules.rule: Default production branch must be 'main'. Preview/staging branch is 'preview'. Never use 'master' for new projects.

rules.reason: 8 of 10 apps already use HTTPS. Two without it (inframanager, MealPlanning) are flagged for remediation.
rules.rule: All production apps with a public FQDN must use HTTPS (https:// in domain config). Only internal utilities without a custom domain (e.g. sslip.io auto-domains) are exempt.

rules.reason: All three compose apps already follow this pattern. Documented March 2026 audit.
rules.rule: Compose apps must define their domain via Traefik labels in docker-compose.yml, not via the Coolify FQDN field. Single-container apps use the Coolify FQDN field.

rules.reason: All compose apps already use this consistently.
rules.rule: Compose services must use restart policy 'unless-stopped'.

rules.reason: All compose apps follow this pattern. Documented March 2026 audit.
rules.rule: Compose apps must use an app-specific Docker network for inter-service communication, with 'coolify' added as an external network for Traefik routing.

rules.reason: Host CPU cannot handle npm build. Causes CPU spikes and stalled Coolify deploys. Always pre-build via GitHub Actions and push image to GHCR.
rules.rule: Never source-build Next.js or any TypeScript/Node app on the VPS via Coolify.

rules.reason: Security. All secrets go in BWS (Bitwarden Secrets Manager). Coolify injects them as environment variables at deploy time.
rules.rule: Never commit secrets, .env files, or API keys to git.

rules.reason: Unpredictable upgrades break reproducibility and can introduce breaking changes silently.
rules.rule: Never use the :latest tag for any Docker image (postgres, redis, node, python, etc.).

rules.reason: Coolify cron running alongside the scheduler sidecar causes duplicated backups, health probes, and restore drills.
rules.rule: Disable Coolify scheduled jobs for Flavor C apps that have an in-stack scheduler sidecar.

rules.reason: No database connection exists at build time. Migrations must run at container startup in the CMD entrypoint.
rules.rule: Never run Alembic migrations at Docker build time (in Dockerfile RUN steps).

rules.reason: Coolify's built-in auto-backup only works for its managed Postgres resources. SQLite backup requires a Coolify cron job calling backup.sh.
rules.rule: Flavor A apps (SQLite) require a manually configured Coolify scheduled backup job.

rules.reason: Redis is queue and cache only. All durable data must live in Postgres. Redis data loss on restart must be acceptable.
rules.rule: Do not use Redis as a primary datastore.

rules.reason: Alpine lacks glibc. Compiled Python dependencies (asyncpg, psycopg2, etc.) fail or require complex workarounds on Alpine.
rules.rule: Use python:3.12-slim, not python:3.12-alpine, as the Python base image.

rules.reason: A mismatch causes silent OAuth failure. Preview deployments need their own callback URI registered in Google Cloud Console.
rules.rule: Google OAuth redirect URIs must match exactly and must be registered per environment (production and preview separately).

rules.reason: Infra Brain is the source of truth. Do not infer standards from existing app code — that code may predate the standard.
rules.rule: Query Infra Brain before pinning any dependency version or making any infrastructure decision.

rules.reason: Standardized March 2026 audit. Replaces inconsistent 8080/8765/80 usage across apps.
rules.rule: Standard exposed ports by stack: Python/FastAPI = 8000 (all flavors). Node/Next.js = 3000. No other ports without documented justification.

rules.reason: Aligns with existing infra-standards skill and observed compose patterns.
rules.rule: Health check path for single-container apps: /api/health. Compose apps use /health/live (liveness) and /health/ready (readiness).

rules.reason: Standardized from audit. Previous defaults (5s interval, 10 retries) were too aggressive.
rules.rule: Coolify-level health check settings: enabled=true, host=127.0.0.1, interval=10s, timeout=5s, retries=5, start_period=15s. Port must be explicitly set to match the app's exposed port.

rules.reason: Discovered March 2026. Auth is keyring-based (no env vars). Token scopes cover full repo CRUD, Actions management, and secret management. 8+ projects already use GitHub Actions workflows.
rules.rule: GitHub CLI (gh v2.88+) is installed and authenticated as AlobarQuest via OS keyring with scopes: repo, workflow, gist, read:org. Use `gh` for all GitHub operations: repo creation, secret management, Actions workflows, PRs, and issues. Do not use curl or raw API calls when gh can handle it.

rules.reason: Aligns with existing infra-brain BLOCK rules: default branch must be main, secrets never committed to git. Pipe syntax prevents secrets from appearing in shell history.
rules.rule: When creating new repos, use `gh repo create alobarquest/<name> --private` and confirm default branch is `main`. Set repo secrets via `gh secret set <NAME> -R alobarquest/<repo>`. Never echo secret values — pipe them: `echo "<value>" | gh secret set <NAME> -R alobarquest/<repo>`.

rules.reason: Discovered March 2026. Enables full automation of secret provisioning during app setup. Pair with openssl/python for value generation.
rules.rule: BWS CLI (bws v2.0.0) is installed at /usr/local/bin/bws and authenticated via BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN env var. Use `bws secret create <KEY> <VALUE> <PROJECT_ID>` to store secrets, `bws secret list` to enumerate, `bws secret get <ID>` to retrieve. Supports json/yaml/env/table output formats. Use this for all secret management — do not ask the user to manually create BWS entries.

rules.reason: Deploy Key is simpler, more secure, and sufficient when Actions handles CI/CD. GitHub App grants broader OAuth access and PR write permissions that are unnecessary when Coolify is just the deployment target. Discovered March 2026 during REDealEngine setup.
rules.rule: For new apps using GitHub Actions CI/CD (Flavor B/C), use Deploy Key (not GitHub App) as the Coolify Git source type. Deploy Key provides single-repo read-only access — minimum privilege. GitHub App is only needed when Coolify itself handles builds, PR previews, or commit status updates.

rules.reason: Open Brain migration attempted coolify_create_application_public for a private repo. App was created but could not pull code. Had to delete and recreate via UI with deploy key.
rules.rule: Do not use coolify_create_application_public for private repos — it creates a public-source app that cannot access private GitHub repos. Use Coolify UI with deploy key or GitHub App source instead, until infraops MCP adds private repo creation tools.

rules.reason: Both env var tools return Validation failed when targeting a compose app UUID. Discovered during Open Brain deployment. Single-container apps work fine.
rules.rule: coolify_create_app_env and coolify_bulk_create_app_envs fail with Validation Error on Docker Compose applications — set env vars via Coolify UI for compose apps until the infraops MCP is fixed.

rules.reason: HTTP-only endpoints expose traffic in plaintext. All production apps must enforce HTTPS.
rules.rule: All Coolify application FQDNs must use HTTPS (not HTTP).

rules.reason: The secret UUID is immutable; the name is a mutable label that will be renamed and break by-name fetches. — FIX: Reference secrets by stable UUID (bws secret get <uuid>), not by name. The UUID is non-secret, so hardcoding it is fine.
rules.rule: bws.reference-by-stable-uuid

rules.reason: Repos that consume BWS secrets must declare which UUIDs they use. — FIX: Add a .bws-secrets.toml declaring the secret UUIDs this repo consumes.
rules.rule: bws.secret-manifest-present

rules.reason: The manifest must match reality or it rots into fiction. — FIX: Add undeclared UUIDs to the manifest; remove stale entries.
rules.rule: bws.manifest-matches-usage

rules.reason: A workload's machine-account should be scoped to only the projects its secrets need. — FIX: Using the manifest's UUIDs, confirm the workload's machine-account is scoped to only the projects those secrets live in.
rules.rule: bws.least-privilege-scope

rules.reason: Preventive gitignore pattern-coverage check, not actual-file exposure; committed secret files are still caught by the bws.no-token-* BLOCK rules.
rules.rule: bws.secret-files-gitignored

rules.reason: Backups run via the vps-backup restic system (NAS + Google Drive offsite + weekly verify), NOT Coolify-native backups, which are unused on this fleet. The infraops audit enriches each coolify_database with a synthetic `backup_covered` field sourced from vps-backup's coverage manifest (~/.infraops/vps-backup-manifest.json: DB UUID -> last successful dump+restic copy). A running DB absent from the manifest has no proven recovery path and is flagged. 'Backup configuration' in the rule text means manifest coverage; the prior check asserted on Coolify's unused native backup_configs field, which was empty on every DB and produced pure noise. See infraops-mcp-server BACKLOG #4 and standards/backup-manifest.ts.
rules.rule: All running Coolify databases must have backup configurations defined.

rules.reason: Health checks are required only on EXPOSED applications — those with an FQDN / proxy routing — where Coolify uses the HTTP health check to route traffic and detect unhealthy containers. Non-exposed background workers (no FQDN; e.g. github-to-bitbucket-mirror, a mirror-then-sleep loop that serves no HTTP) cannot pass an HTTP health check, so requiring one produced a permanently-unsatisfiable finding that re-escalated every scan. The guard was changed from 'status contains running' to 'fqdn non_empty' so workers with no domain are correctly out of scope. A worker may still be given a process/command-level check manually, but it is not required by this rule. (Was: asserted health_check_enabled on every running app regardless of exposure.)
rules.rule: Health checks must be enabled on all running Coolify applications.

rules.reason: Credentials must rotate before their class max age: GitHub PAT (classic or fine-grained) 180d, provider API key (OpenRouter/OpenAI/etc.) 365d, BWS machine token 365d, brain MCP key 365d. Age anchors to created/last_rotated in the repo's .cred-consumers.toml (or the rotation state's lastRotated). Surfaced nightly by the infraops security-drift 3AM scan as a source=security change-manager item (WARN → NORMAL tier); executor-assisted rotation runs only after Devon approves. — FIX: rotate via the WS-0.7 lane: Devon mints the replacement at the provider console (create is ALWAYS human), stages it in Keychain item cred-rotation/<cred-id>, approves in change-manager; the 4AM no-LLM executor then stores (quarantine old + edit keeper BWS secret in place), deploys to all mapped consumers, verifies (provider 200 + consumer health), and only retires after the old value probes dead (401). NEVER revoke-first.
rules.rule: cred.rotation-age

rules.reason: A committed BWS machine-account token is a credential leak. — FIX: Remove the token; move it to a gitignored env file sourced at runtime; ROTATE the exposed token.
rules.rule: bws.no-token-in-tracked-files

rules.reason: Git history retains a token even after it is removed from the working tree. — FIX: Rotate/revoke the token; optionally scrub history with git filter-repo.
rules.rule: bws.no-token-in-git-history

rules.reason: The bootstrap BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN must never be inline in committed config. — FIX: Source BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN from a gitignored env file; never inline it in a plist/compose/script.
rules.rule: bws.bootstrap-token-not-inline

rules.reason: A recorded exposure event (leaked to logs/transcripts/history) makes a credential rotate-NOW regardless of age: declare it as a [[credential.exposure]] entry in the owning repo's .cred-consumers.toml; the 3AM security-drift scan emits a one-shot URGENT source=security finding per open exposure and it clears ONLY when the revoke is confirmed (old value probes 401 and is retired by the executor, or Devon records it via `security-drift-cli resolve-exposure` when no probe-able copy exists). Purging the plaintext never closes an exposure — revoke/reissue does. FAIL-SAFE: rotation never revokes a credential whose consumer set is not attested (consumers_verified sweep date in .cred-consumers.toml). Seeded 2026-07-02 with the 5 live ~/.codex-leaked creds (2 GitHub classic PATs, 1 fine-grained PAT, 1 OpenRouter generic key, 1 OpenAI project key — identities in ~/docs/security-audit/2026-07-02-codex-leak-rotation-targets.md).
rules.rule: cred.exposure-rotate
